landing.point2: Safety team, hazardous materials, equipment and on-site map
landing.point3: Versioned documents: safety file, safety plan and safety data sheets
landing.point4: Digital safety certificate, verifiable by anyone

landing.emergencyBody: This portal does not replace a call. Dial directly:

It is not an official certificate of the National Office of Civil Protection or of any other administration, and it does not replace the permits and inspections required by law.
verify.sealBody: A picture of the Office's electronic signature above, as printed on the PDF. Its value comes from the signature, not the picture.

2026-11.intro: e-Himaya is the national platform for reporting emergencies to the Civil Protection.

sections.title: 1. Purpose
sections.body: e-Himaya is a digital platform of the National Civil Protection Office ("the Office") for reporting emergencies and following them up. These terms govern the relationship between the Office and the users of the mobile app and the institutions portal.

sections.title: 2. Our mission
sections.body: To protect lives and property, and to rebuild trust between citizens and Civil Protection through direct and open communication. Describing the incident accurately and showing the scene as it is shortens response time and makes the intervention more effective.

sections.title: 3. Nature and limits of the service
sections.body:
3.1 The app complements 198 and does not replace it. In immediate danger, call 198 directly.
3.2 The app gives no medical advice; its safety tips are for general awareness and do not replace the instructions of Civil Protection staff.
3.3 It depends on factors outside the Office's control: mobile network and internet coverage, location signal, battery and the condition of the phone. The Office aims for the highest availability and fixes faults as fast as possible.

sections.title: 4. User obligations
sections.body:
4.1 Use the app in good faith and only for real emergencies; give accurate, up-to-date information, especially your phone number.
4.2 Keep location turned on and use the latest version of the app.
4.3 Do not put yourself in danger to film, and follow the instructions of responders.
4.4 Do not harm, disrupt, bypass the protections of, or reverse-engineer the app.

sections.title: 5. False alarms and misuse
sections.body: Every report sends out rescue teams that other lives may need at the same moment. A deliberate false report or any misuse of the app exposes its author to prosecution under Tunisian law, and may lead to temporary or permanent suspension of the account or of reporting from the device concerned.

sections.title: 6. Institutions' obligations
sections.body: A registered institution provides accurate, up-to-date information on its identity, activity, buildings and managers, and is responsible for it. Filing and updating the evacuation plan and building plans makes the intervention easier and shortens search and rescue inside the building. The account is activated only after the Office approves it.

sections.title: 7. Volunteers
sections.body: Volunteer status is granted only after the Office approves it. Volunteers follow the operations room's instructions and act only within the task assigned to them.

sections.title: 8. Personal data protection
sections.body:
8.1 Personal data is processed under Organic Law No. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 on the protection of personal data, under the supervision of the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (INPDP), solely to handle emergencies and to keep you informed about your reports.
8.2 When you send a report, the Office receives your position, the type of incident, the description and attached media, and your account details if you have an account.
8.3 Emergency contacts and the text of your SOS message are stored encrypted on your phone only and are never sent to the Office.
8.4 You can report without an account under a pseudonym; your IP address is not recorded.
8.5 Only authorised staff can access the data, which is kept as long as needed to handle the case and meet legal obligations. You have the right to access, correct and object to the processing of your data.

sections.title: 9. Changes to the app and these terms
sections.body: The Office may improve the app or change these terms. You are told about each new version and what it contains, and asked to accept again when the terms change.

sections.title: 10. Applicable law
sections.body: These terms are governed by Tunisian law; Tunisian courts have jurisdiction over any dispute.
